tagline: We deliver smart, easy-to-use solutions that manage solar generation, storage and communication on one platform.
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of microinverters shipped is the primary indicator of market penetration and growth of the Enphase system, which relies on an integrated and scalable platform. It is the fundamental driver of the installed base and future software services.

kpis.name: Microinverters Shipped
kpis.explanation: Total number of microinverters shipped to customers, a key indicator of physical growth.
kpis.description: Enphase shipped approximately 86.4 million microinverters as of December 31, 2025, reflecting widespread global adoption.

kpis.name: Deployed Systems
kpis.explanation: Number of residential and commercial systems installed worldwide.
kpis.description: More than 5.1 million Enphase systems have been deployed in over 160 countries as of December 31, 2025.
kpis.signal: Over 5 million Enphase systems in service

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of products sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved in 2025, supported by enhanced operational efficiency, qualification for US tax credits (Section 48E, AMPTC) and reduction in component costs.
kpis.signal: Margin improvement through domestic manufacturing and federal tax credits

kpis.name: R&D Intensity
kpis.explanation: Research and development spending as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Enphase maintains R&D spending at 12% of revenue, focused on system integration, power electronics and embedded software.
kpis.signal: Consistent investment in product innovation and system integration

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on equipment and infrastructure to support growth.
kpis.description: CAPEX in 2025 supported expansion of domestic manufacturing capacity (internal facility and Flex partnership) to benefit from federal tax credits and domestic content bonus.
kpis.signal: CAPEX targeted at US domestic manufacturing

kpis.name: Total Employees
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Enphase had approximately 3,200 employees at end of 2025, with sustained growth driven by R&D investments, customer support and domestic manufacturing expansion.
kpis.signal: Measured headcount growth aligned with R&D and customer support needs

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 3.51 billion euros in latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 1.21 billion euros in latest year

kpis.name: US Manufacturing Capacity
kpis.explanation: Quarterly production capacity for microinverters in the United States.
kpis.description: Combined US manufacturing capacity (internal facility and Flex partnership) reaches 5 million microinverters per quarter, supporting access to domestic tax credits Section 48E and AMPTC, and qualification for domestic content bonus (45% FEOC).
kpis.signal: US capacity stabilized at 5 million microinverters per quarter

kpis.name: Safe Harbor Agreements
kpis.explanation: Agreements concluded with solar lease financing companies (TPO) for lease credit arrangements and power purchase agreements.
kpis.description: Enphase signed multiple Safe Harbor agreements in 2025 with solar and battery financing companies to support residential growth through TPO partnerships, reflecting a strategic growth channel following the expiration of Section 25D tax credit on December 31, 2025 introduced by OBBBA.
kpis.signal: Increased engagement in TPO segment following expiration of residential Section 25D ITC

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company has a dedicated cybersecurity committee and procedures in place, but cybersecurity risks remain present. A cybersecurity subcommittee has been established within the Audit Committee, led by a member with cybersecurity expertise. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Litigation
risks.score_rationale: The company is involved in several litigations, including class action lawsuits and legal proceedings that may impact finances and reputation. (Item 3)

risks.title: Regulation and Legislative Framework
risks.score_rationale: The adoption of OBBBA in July 2025 introduced material changes to tax credit programs: expiration of Section 25D (Dec 31, 2025), new FEOC requirements (45% domestic threshold), future ITC reductions (storage 75% in 2034, 50% in 2035, 0% in 2036), and deadlines for Section 48E (solar projects 12 months to begin construction, placed in service by Dec 31, 2027). (Item 7, MD&A)

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive market for microinverters and home energy systems. Must maintain its differentiated technology position (integrated system approach vs string inverters) to remain competitive. (Item 1, Business)

risks.title: Supply Chain and Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: The company relies on critical suppliers concentrated geographically. LFP cells for batteries are sourced exclusively from two suppliers in China, despite active exploration of alternatives. Adoption of US domestic manufacturing does not fully resolve dependence on imported components. (Item 7, MD&A)

risks.title: Reputation and Brand Image
risks.score_rationale: The company may be affected by reputational issues in case of litigation or non-compliance with federal tax credit requirements (FEOC, domestic content). Increased exposure through safe harbor agreements and TPO expansion raises reputation risk surface. (Item 3, Item 7)

risks.title: Geopolitics and Trade Tensions
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in over 160 countries and is exposed to geopolitical risks, evolving trade tariffs and US regulatory uncertainties related to trade. Critical dependencies on Asian components (LFP, semiconductors) amplify this exposure. (Item 7, MD&A)
